This pack's income-and-resources supplement corrects a $2,750 non-elderly/disabled resource-limit figure several secondary sources repeat, in favor of Montana DPHHS's own currently-published $3,000 figure (SNAP 400, effective 10/01/2024). This correction tracks the federal general SNAP resource-limit COLA increase from $2,750 (FFY2024) to $3,000 (FFY2025 and current FFY2026). Re-verify against DPHHS's own SNAP 400 page directly after the FFY2027 COLA cycle begins (10/01/2026) before restating either figure with full confidence beyond that date.

This pack's criminal-justice-disqualifications supplement rests on the exact 'not complying with conditions of supervision' modifier text this pack found consistently in three separate DPHHS SNAP manual sections (SNAP 001, SNAP 304-1, SNAP 602-4) — a genuinely cross-checked finding within DPHHS's own manual — but this pack did NOT find a standalone Montana Code Annotated statute or Administrative Rule of Montana section stating this modifier in as many words (the MCA Title 53, Chapter 2, Part 9 sections index this pack directly fetched contains no drug-felony provision at all). Re-verify this modifier's continued operative status directly against a current DPHHS manual fetch, or by contacting a local Office of Public Assistance, before treating it as settled beyond this window.

This pack's confirmed dollar figures (Standard Deduction $209/$209/$209/$223/$261/$299, Standard Utility Allowance $799, Limited Utility Allowance $267, One Utility Allowance $116, Telephone Allowance $34, Medical Expense Deduction threshold $35, resource limits $4,500/$3,000, and the income-eligibility tables by household size at 130%/100%/200%/165% FPG) are drawn from Montana DPHHS's current SNAP 001 (effective 10/01/2025-09/30/2026) and SNAP 602-2/602-4 (effective 10/01/2024 and 10/01/2025 respectively), matching the current FFY2026 cycle.
